## 1. What was read

**921 research articles** from 33 of the 33 journals on the roster, filtered to `journal article` and excluding reviews, editorials, news, comment and case reports.

| General | Cancer | Immune | Bioinfo | Sysbio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 427 | 134 | 84 | 254 | 22 |

!!! warning "Volume swing against the median month: cancer -30%"
    Check the source before reading anything into this. Two benign causes account for most of these. `bioinfo` every January carries the Nucleic Acids Research database issue and runs high. And several journals simply deposit nothing in some months — queried directly, PubMed returns zero *Nucleic Acids Research* research articles dated 2025-12, and zero *Bioinformatics* in 2024-04, 2025-01, 2025-04 and 2026-03. Those holes are in the source and are reproduced exactly by re-running the harvest, so a swing here is not evidence that a field went quiet and is not usually evidence that the pipeline broke either.

Largest contributors: Nature 106, Nucleic Acids Res 98, JAMA 90, Science 79, Bioinformatics 66, Cell 41.

## 3. The evidence that moved it

**Clinical-AI limitations, in a *Nature Medicine* title, in September 2024.**
[38965432](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38965432/): evaluation and mitigation of the **limitations** of large
language models in clinical decision-making. The corpus's 2025-08 briefing was
built on a claimed "inversion" in which clinical AI turned negative that summer;
that briefing has already been withdrawn, on the grounds that no title in all of
2025 stated a null for any AI intervention. This paper shows the counterweight
was in the flagship clinical venue a year before the inversion was supposed to
have happened.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

Nothing lands on a tracked thread this month. September 2024 is the quietest
month in the 2024 half of the corpus for thread-relevant refutations, and since
2024 was read thread-first rather than exhaustively, that should be read as a
limit on the reading rather than a fact about the month.

### (b) Method credibility

[39322959](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39322959/) (*Genome Biol*): a realistic benchmark for differential-abundance
testing **and confounder adjustment** in human microbiome studies — the direct
methodological successor to May's *Nature Medicine* confounders paper, four
months later, and evidence that the objection was taken up rather than absorbed.

[39227979](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39227979/): a multiple-imputation procedure **outperforms** complete-case
and single imputation in differential expression. The default handling of missing
data in the standard pipeline is wrong.

[39152037](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39152037/) (*Genome Res*): a **simple** method for finding related sequences
by adding probabilities of alternative alignments. Simple-beats-complex again,
and this is the third instance in 2024 alone — January's linear brain dynamics,
March's convolutions, September's alignment probabilities. A genre this corpus
first recorded as a 2026 phenomenon is running at roughly one paper a quarter in
2024.
